cross_condition_results: The locally retained cross-condition summary reports T-FNO minus U-Net as GWRMSE +0.09448 (95% CI [+0.04363, +0.14534]); Interface-temperature RMSE +0.61497 (95% CI [+0.31906, +0.90941]); Interface-temperature-jump MAE +0.18985 (95% CI [+0.18080, +0.19935]); Mass-conservation MAE +0.01429 (95% CI [+0.00915, +0.02085]). Every unadjusted exact two-sided p-value is .0625 (the minimum attainable at n=5) and every Holm-adjusted p-value is 1.0. The stored directions consistently favor U-Net, including on mass conservation, but this descriptive five-seed/two-trajectory check is statistically underpowered and does not establish a cross-condition ranking.

hybrid_results:
The checkpoint-retaining CUDA rerun used the same 11 paired seeds, prepared tensors, and immutable T-FNO/U-Net baseline checkpoints as Section 4.1; baseline-metric identity was verified before the intervention analysis. The zero-penalty local-global hybrid was non-inferior to T-FNO on interface-temperature RMSE (Holm p=.00146484) and jump MAE (Holm p=.00146484), but failed mass-conservation non-inferiority to U-Net (hybrid minus U-Net +0.04152, 95% CI [+0.03611, +0.04632], Holm p=1). A local receptive field alone therefore did not recover U-Net's conservation behavior.

With the frozen $\lambda_{\mathrm{div}}=0.30$ intervention, the divergence hybrid passed the predeclared one-metric mass-conservation non-inferiority gate: mean mass MAE 0.09528 versus 0.16562 for U-Net, paired difference $-0.07034$, 95% CI $[-0.07454, -0.06654]$, exact one-sided p=.000488281. The fresh CUDA rerun did not establish an interface regression relative to the zero-penalty hybrid. This is a confirmatory tutorial-split result only; no divergence-hybrid numerical claim is made for the independent cross-condition split.
tutorial_results: Across 11 paired seeds, T-FNO was significantly worse on mass-conservation MAE (+0.04917, 95% paired bootstrap CI [+0.04448, +0.05386], unadjusted p=.000976562, Holm p=.0214844). No overall GWRMSE winner was established (T-FNO − U-Net: +0.00460, 95% paired bootstrap CI [-0.05759, +0.05894], sign-flip p=.890625, Holm p=1). T-FNO showed no statistically significant advantage on interface-temperature RMSE (-0.18853, 95% CI [-0.47490, +0.06732], unadjusted p=.234375, Holm p=1) or interface-temperature-jump MAE (-0.09277, 95% CI [-0.22032, +0.02548], unadjusted p=.196289, Holm p=1). Thus, the fixed-split evidence supports a conservation weakness for T-FNO, without a confirmed offsetting interface-fidelity benefit.
